import cv2
import numpy as np
import json
import math
from triangulate import get_bearing, intersect_rays

with open('/work/poses.json') as f:
    poses = json.load(f)

# Sideboard:
# Frame 1: bottom-right
# Frame 14: bottom-right
# Frame 18: bottom-left
# Frame 19: bottom-right
# Frame 20: center-bottom

# Let's inspect cabinet front color:
# In Frame 20:
img20 = cv2.imread('/work/observations/obs_0020.png')
# Cabinet front is beige:
# around x=200..400, y=360..500
# Cabinet top is light grey:
# around x=200..400, y=340..370
print("Cabinet front color in 20:", img20[420, 250].tolist())
print("Cabinet top color in 20:", img20[355, 250].tolist())

# Detect sideboard in Frame 20, 19, 14, 18
for f in [14, 18, 19, 20]:
    img = cv2.imread(f'/work/observations/obs_{f:04d}.png')
    # cabinet front: R ~ 180-210, G ~ 160-180, B ~ 130-160
    # Let's use mask:
    mask = (img[:, :, 2] > 170) & (img[:, :, 2] < 220) & \
           (img[:, :, 1] > 140) & (img[:, :, 1] < 190) & \
           (img[:, :, 0] > 120) & (img[:, :, 0] < 170)
    ys, xs = np.where(mask)
    if len(xs) > 100:
        print(f"Sideboard in {f}: x in [{xs.min()}, {xs.max()}], y in [{ys.min()}, {ys.max()}], center_x = {np.mean(xs):.1f}")
